evidence: Workbook Quality Checks!A16:D16 requires a pinned agent image; the frozen skill quality-checks.md:66-68 specifically says pinned base. Frozen task/environment/Dockerfile:1 uses FROM node:22-bookworm-slim without an immutable digest. That mutable tag can resolve to different Node/Debian base bytes on a later build. The same line appears in frozen template/environment/Dockerfile:1, so this is a template-controlled defect requiring an authorized template-level correction, not a task-only divergence. Other row conditions are supported: Dockerfile:3-13 sets NODE_PATH, installs express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 at image build, and stages/chmods instructions and assets; Dockerfile:14-23 creates and git-initializes /app with .gitkeep; there is no COPY of solution or tests. The indexed full-install-binding.json SHA256 matches the current artifact (see evidence/15/source-audit.json); its scripted run reports Node v22.23.2, globally resolved better-sqlite3 12.4.1, no local node_modules, health 200, and passed=true. It demonstrates one successful current build/install, not an immutable future build or configured grading.
counterexample: A conforming app using the promised Node 22/Express/SQLite server can work against the cached image today yet fail after the mutable node:22-bookworm-slim tag moves to a different Node or Debian patch level that changes the native better-sqlite3 build/runtime environment. An app serving only static content could still run, so current health or a simple app success would not reveal this reproducibility defect.
suggested_fix: Pin the shared agent-image base to an immutable digest, record the selected Node 22/Debian image, and rebuild and rerun the install smoke on a new frozen candidate.
